title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Specimen Cabinet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Specimen Cabinet
options.lineage: natural-history collection drawers, specimen labels and colour-headed pins
options.thesis: Every port is a catalogued specimen: one drawer per game, an accession label per fork, a coloured pin for its status.
options.viewport: Cabinet-green top bar with search; filter rail of drawers (games), platforms and pin colours; main field packs typed specimen labels edge to edge inside the open Bloodborne drawer, upstream bbport pinned first as the type specimen.
options.risk: Pushed too far the museum reads as costume; it must stay a fast filterable list with standard inputs.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears: archived or vanished repos stay in the drawer, stamped DEACCESSIONED.
Every quantity (stars, days since last push, release) set in tabular figures in fixed label fields.
Density courage: labels pack edge to edge, a whole drawer readable in one viewport.
The link colour appears only on things you can open: repo, release, filters.
Drawer compartments are the visible layout grid, not decoration.
One motion duration for every state change: filter, open drawer, pin.

options.label: The Compatibility List
options.lineage: emulator compatibility tables (RPCS3, Dolphin, ProtonDB tiers)
options.thesis: The scene's own reference format: one dense row per port, a tier bar for status.
options.viewport: Search across the top, filter chips below, a sortable table with a coloured tier bar on the left edge of each row.
options.risk: Familiar: this is what most compat lists, and most runs in this category, already look like.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Friendly cards on a warm ground, one bright action colour.
options.viewport: Single column of soft cards with a bottom tab bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: enthusiast porters do not read as a consumer app, and one-idea cards waste density.
options.kept: Action colour reserved strictly for actionable elements.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Hundreds of stamp-size entries keyed by table code.
options.viewport: Packed thumbnail grid with a hall map.
options.case: Close on audience, loses on clarity: it needs per-entry artwork the ports do not have.
options.kept: Density courage: many entries per screen.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.viewport: Stacked coupons, one leg per sheet.
options.case: A catalog is not a journey; the sequence metaphor misleads.
options.kept: States stamp themselves; nothing disappears, it cancels.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid letters over a small grotesk list.
options.case: Poster ambition with no tie to games or porting.
options.kept: The layout grid stays visible as structure.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.viewport: One lobe per screen with capsule controls.
options.case: Playful geography fights a scan-and-filter task.
options.kept: One motion timing for everything that moves.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.lineage: printer's exposure cards and zone ramps
options.thesis: Translucent sheets with hatch density as load.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets over a zone wedge.
options.case: Elegant but foreign to players; hatching hides simple status.
options.kept: Quantities in tabular figures in fixed fields.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark gaming-catalog grid of cards with one neon accent.
canonCard.viewport: Hero search, filter pills, a three-column card grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every gaming index by design.
